body_text: When people think about what makes a property successful, the conversation often centers on occupancy, leasing, amenities, location, and revenue. But behind every well-run property is a team making sure everything actually works. And when something unexpected happens, someone knows what to do. That someone is often a maintenance professional. Maintenance teams may not always be the most visible people in real estate, but their impact can be felt throughout a property and on the bottom line. They are problem-solvers, customer service professionals, safety advocates, operational experts, and often the first line of defense against costly property issues. What a Maintenance Professional Actually Does They Protect the Property and Its Value A property is a significant investment, and maintenance professionals play a critical role in protecting that investment every day. Routine inspections, preventative maintenance, timely repairs, and attention to small issues can help prevent larger and more expensive problems down the road. A minor plumbing issue caught early is very different from a major water event. A small HVAC concern addressed proactively is preferable to a system failure in the middle of extreme weather. Maintenance isn't simply about fixing what's broken; it's about preventing what's next. That proactive mindset can help extend the life of equipment, reduce unexpected expenses, and preserve the condition and value of the property. They Directly Impact the Resident and Tenant Experience For residents and commercial tenants, the quality of a property isn't measured solely by its finishes or amenities. It's also measured by what happens when something goes wrong. How quickly is a maintenance request addressed? Is the problem resolved correctly? Is someone communicating with the resident or tenant throughout the process? Maintenance professionals are often directly responsible for these moments. A fast, professional response can turn a frustrating experience into one that builds trust. On the other hand, unresolved maintenance issues can quickly affect satisfaction, reputation, renewals, and retention. In many ways, maintenance is customer service. They Know the Property Better Than Almost Anyone Maintenance professionals develop an incredible level of institutional knowledge in their work. They know which HVAC units tend to need attention. They know the quirks of an older building. They know where a recurring leak starts. They know which equipment is approaching the end of its useful life. They also notice things other people may miss. A maintenance professional walking through a property might spot a dripping pipe, unusual equipment noise, damaged flooring, a safety concern, or another issue before it becomes a major problem. That knowledge is incredibly valuable. They're not simply responding to work orders. They're building a working understanding of the property every day. They Help Control Costs When budgets are tight, maintenance can sometimes be viewed as an expense to minimize. But the right maintenance strategy can actually help control costs. Preventative maintenance can reduce emergency repairs. Proper equipment care can extend useful life. Addressing issues early can help avoid expensive damage. And experienced maintenance professionals can often identify practical solutions that balance immediate needs with long-term property goals. They Keep Properties Moving Real estate is an operational business. A property can't function effectively if critical systems aren't working, spaces aren't safe, or residents and tenants aren't getting the service they expect. Maintenance professionals help keep all of those moving parts operating behind the scenes. And when something unexpected happens—as it inevitably does in real estate—they are often the people expected to respond quickly, troubleshoot the issue, and find a solution. That requires technical knowledge, adaptability, communication skills, and composure under pressure. They Are Problem-Solvers at Heart Maintenance work is rarely as simple as following a checklist. Every property presents different challenges. Every building has its own history. Every repair can reveal another problem. Maintenance professionals have to diagnose issues, make decisions, prioritize competing requests, and sometimes find creative solutions with limited time or resources. That's a valuable skill set in any industry. In real estate, where unexpected problems can quickly become expensive ones, it's indispensable. Investing in Maintenance Means Investing in the Property The value of maintenance professionals goes far beyond completed work orders. They protect assets. They support resident and tenant satisfaction. They help control costs. They contribute to safety. They preserve property standards. And they provide the expertise that keeps properties operating day after day. That's why maintenance shouldn't be viewed as simply another line item in the operating budget. It's an investment in the people who protect the investment. The next time you walk through a property and everything looks, feels, and works exactly as it should, remember: there's a good chance someone in maintenance helped make that happen. The right maintenance professionals don’t just fix problems—they protect your assets, support your residents and tenants, control costs, and keep your property moving forward. When you need experienced maintenance talent you can count on, BG Staffing can help you build the team behind a better-performing property.

title: Wedding Invitation Etiquette: Rules, Wording & Timeline
summary: Wedding invitation etiquette calls for mailing invitations 6 to 8 weeks before a local wedding and 10 to 12 weeks before a destination event. Every
body_text: Last Updated on August 10, 2026 by Joy Editors Wedding invitation etiquette calls for mailing invitations 6 to 8 weeks before a local wedding and 10 to 12 weeks before a destination event. Every invitation should include the host line, couple names, date, time, venue, and RSVP details. Registry information belongs on your wedding website, not the invitation itself. Address outer envelopes using full formal names and titles. Set the RSVP deadline 3 to 4 weeks before the wedding day. Digital invitations are now widely accepted for casual and semi-formal celebrations. Getting the details right on your wedding invitations is one of those planning tasks that feels simple until you sit down to do it. Whose name goes first? Do you spell out the time? Is a digital RSVP card acceptable? This guide covers every rule, from traditional wording conventions to the modern updates couples are embracing in 2026. Whether you are hosting a black-tie ballroom affair or a casual backyard celebration, you will find the etiquette guidance you need below. What Every Wedding Invitation Must Include Before diving into wording nuances, make sure your invitation covers these six essential elements. Missing even one creates confusion for guests and extra follow-up for you. The Host Line The host line tells guests who is extending the invitation. Traditionally, whoever funds the wedding is listed as the host. Here are the most common formats: One set of parents hosting: “Mr. and Mrs. Robert Smith request the honor of your presence” Both families hosting: “Mr. and Mrs. Robert Smith and Mr. and Mrs. James Johnson request the pleasure of your company” Couple hosting themselves: “Together with their families, Sarah Smith and Michael Johnson invite you to celebrate their marriage” No specific host: “Together with their families” is a graceful catch-all when multiple parties contribute or when you prefer not to single anyone out The Couple’s Names Name order on a wedding invitation is a personal choice. Traditional etiquette placed the bride’s name first, and many couples still follow that convention. Others list names alphabetically, by syllable flow, or in whichever order feels most natural. For same-sex couples, the same flexibility applies. Use full first and last names on formal invitations, and skip middle names unless they are a meaningful part of someone’s identity. One formatting note: if one partner’s parents are listed on the host line, use only that partner’s first and middle name (since they share the parent’s surname). The other partner’s name includes their title and full name. Date and Time Formatting Formal invitations spell out every element. Write “Saturday, the fifteenth of June, two thousand and twenty-six” rather than using numerals. For time, use “at six o’clock in the evening” or “at half after five o’clock.” Semi-formal and casual invitations can use a shorter format: “June 15, 2026 at 5:30 PM.” Always include the day of the week. It helps guests double-check their calendars and reduces errors. Venue and Location List the venue name on one line and the city and state on the next. Street addresses are optional on the invitation itself (guests can find directions on your wedding website ). For religious ceremonies, use the full name of the house of worship. RSVP Details The RSVP line is essential. At minimum, include a response deadline. Traditional wording uses “The favour of a reply is requested by the twentieth of May,” while modern invitations often print “RSVP by May 20” or direct guests to an online RSVP page . Editorial tip: Pairing a paper RSVP card with a digital response option gives guests flexibility and simplifies your tracking. With Joy, you can set up an online RSVP page that collects meal preferences, song requests, plus-one names, and dietary needs in one step, so you spend less time chasing responses and more time enjoying the countdown. When to Send Wedding Invitations Timing your invitations well gives guests enough notice without sending so early that the date slips their minds. What to Send Local Wedding Destination Wedding Save-the-Date 6 to 8 months before 8 to 12 months before Formal Invitation 6 to 8 weeks before 10 to 12 weeks before RSVP Deadline 3 to 4 weeks before 4 to 6 weeks before Standard Timeline: 6 to 8 Weeks For a local wedding (most guests within driving distance), mail invitations 6 to 8 weeks before the ceremony. This gives guests time to plan, book accommodations if needed, and RSVP without feeling rushed. Destination Wedding Timeline: 10 to 12 Weeks Destination weddings require more lead time. Guests need to book flights, request time off, and arrange travel logistics. Send these invitations 10 to 12 weeks in advance, following save-the-dates sent 6 to 8 months before the event. Coordinating with Save-the-Dates Save-the-dates should arrive 6 to 8 months before the wedding (up to 12 months for destination events). They are not formal invitations, so keep them simple: names, date, city, and a note that a formal invitation will follow. Include your wedding website URL so guests can start checking details early. Editorial tip: Your save-the-date is the first touchpoint guests have with your wedding. Including a link to your wedding website at this stage lets guests bookmark travel info, accommodation suggestions, and event details months before the formal invitation arrives. With Joy, your website is live as soon as you set it up, so there is no reason to wait. How to Address Wedding Invitation Envelopes Envelope addressing is where many couples feel the most pressure to get things “right.” The good news: the rules are straightforward once you know them. Outer Envelope Rules The outer envelope uses full formal names and titles. No abbreviations except Mr., Mrs., Ms., and Dr. Write out “Street,” “Avenue,” and state names in full. Examples: Married couple (same last name): Mr. and Mrs. David Chen Married couple (different last names): Ms. Lauren Hayes and Mr. David Chen Unmarried couple living together: Ms. Lauren Hayes / Mr. David Chen (each on a separate line) Single guest with plus-one: Ms. Lauren Hayes and Guest Family with children: Mr. and Mrs. David Chen (children named on inner envelope) For a deeper dive with more examples, our guide on how to address wedding invitations covers every scenario. Inner Envelope Rules Inner envelopes are less formal and serve a practical purpose: they clarify exactly who in the household is invited. Skip titles and use first names or informal references: Married couple: David and Lauren Family with children: David, Lauren, Emma, and Jack Guest with plus-one: Lauren and Guest Many modern couples skip the inner envelope entirely. A single-envelope approach saves on printing and postage costs without breaking any major etiquette rules, and it has become increasingly common. Addressing Specific Situations Doctors: Use “Doctor” (or “Dr.”) before the name. If both partners are doctors, write “The Doctors Chen” or “Dr. Lauren Hayes and Dr. David Chen.” Military titles: Active-duty service members use their rank in place of Mr./Mrs. “Captain Lauren Hayes and Mr. David Chen.” Judges and elected officials: Use the full title: “The Honorable Lauren Hayes and Mr. David Chen.” Pro tip: collecting guest addresses is one of the earliest tasks you can tackle. A guest list manager lets you gather mailing addresses digitally and export them when you are ready to print envelopes. Wedding Invitation Wording by Host The wording of your invitation sets the tone for the entire event. A few key phrases signal whether the celebration will be formal, relaxed, or somewhere in between. Parents of One Partner Hosting This is the most traditional format. The hosting parents are named on the host line, and the other partner is introduced with their full title and name. Mr. and Mrs. Robert Allen Smith request the honor of your presence at the marriage of their daughter Sarah Elizabeth to Mr. Michael Thomas Johnson Saturday, the fifteenth of June two thousand and twenty-six at six o’clock in the evening St. Mary’s Cathedral San Francisco, California Note the phrase “honor of your presence.” This is reserved for ceremonies held in a house of worship. For secular venues, use “pleasure of your company.” Both Families Hosting Mr. and Mrs. Robert Smith and Mr. and Mrs. James Johnson request the pleasure of your company at the marriage of Sarah Elizabeth Smith and Michael Thomas Johnson When both families host, list the families in whichever order you prefer and include full names for both partners. Some couples follow the tradition of listing one family first; others go alphabetically. Couple Hosting Themselves Together with their families, Sarah Smith and Michael Johnson invite you to celebrate their marriage This format works well for couples funding their own wedding or those who want to acknowledge all families without listing names individually. It reads as warm and inclusive. Divorced or Remarried Parents When the hosting parents are divorced, list the mother first (traditionally), each on a separate line. Do not connect their names with “and,” since they are no longer a couple: Mrs. Patricia Smith and Mr. Robert Smith request the pleasure of your company at the marriage of their daughter Sarah Elizabeth Honoring a Deceased Parent There is no single right way to honor a parent who has passed. Some couples include a memorial line: “the late Mr. Robert Smith.” Others prefer a separate note inside the invitation or a moment during the ceremony itself. For more wording examples and templates, check out our complete wedding invitation wording guide . RSVP Card and Response Etiquette The RSVP process is where logistics meet courtesy. Getting this right saves you from chasing down responses in the weeks before your wedding. What to Include on RSVP Cards A standard RSVP card includes: A blank line for the guest’s name (prefilled with “M____” for titles, though many couples now skip the M line) Accept and decline checkboxes or lines Number of guests attending Meal choice (if applicable) Response deadline Keep the RSVP card simple. Song requests, dietary restrictions, and other details are better collected through a digital form on your wedding website. Setting the Response Deadline Set the RSVP deadline 3 to 4 weeks before the wedding. This gives you enough time to finalize seating charts, catering numbers, and place cards. For destination weddings, push the deadline to 4 to 6 weeks before the event. Digital RSVP Options Digital RSVPs are increasingly popular, even alongside paper invitations. Many couples include a QR code on their paper RSVP card that links to their wedding website, where guests can respond, select meal options, and provide additional details all in one step. The advantage of a digital system is real-time tracking. You can see who has responded, send reminders to those who have not, and make adjustments without spreadsheets or sticky notes. Handling Non-Responses Some guests will inevitably miss the RSVP deadline. Here is a tactful approach: One week after the deadline: Send a friendly text or call. “We are finalizing our headcount and want to make sure we have a seat for you.” Two weeks after: Follow up once more. If you still receive no response, it is reasonable to assume they are not attending. Mark your list accordingly: You need final numbers for your caterer, so do not leave these spots open indefinitely. Suite Assembly and Mailing Once every piece is printed and addressed, the final step is assembling and mailing your invitation suite. A clean assembly process ensures invitations arrive in pristine condition. Stacking Order for the Invitation Suite Place items face-up in size order, largest to smallest: Invitation (bottom, largest piece) Reception card (if the ceremony and reception are at different locations) Details card (accommodations, transportation, dress code) RSVP card tucked under the flap of its envelope If using an inner envelope, slide the assembled stack inside with the text facing the back flap. Then place the inner envelope inside the outer envelope, with the guest names facing you as you open the flap. Postage and Return Address Bring a fully assembled invitation to the post office for weighing before buying stamps. Square invitations, oversized envelopes, and heavy cardstock often require extra postage. Non-machinable surcharges apply to rigid, lumpy, or non-standard-sized mail, so check current USPS rates before purchasing stamps in bulk. The return address goes on the back flap of the outer envelope (for formal invitations) or the upper left corner of the front (for casual ones). Use the address where you want RSVP cards returned, which may differ from your home address. Do not forget to include a stamped, pre-addressed return envelope with the RSVP card. Making it easy for guests to respond improves your response rate significantly. Hand Delivery vs. Mailing Hand-delivering invitations is a lovely gesture for local guests, but mail them through the post office to any guest who lives out of town. Avoid dropping hand-delivered invitations directly into a mailbox without postage, as this can violate postal regulations. Guest-Related Invitation Etiquette Some of the trickiest etiquette questions involve who gets invited, who gets a plus-one, and how to handle sensitive guest list decisions. Plus-One Rules Standard etiquette guidelines: Always gets a plus-one: Married couples, engaged couples, and couples who live together Typically gets a plus-one: Guests in long-term relationships (6+ months), guests who will not know anyone else at the event Optional: Single guests. Budget and venue capacity usually determine this call When extending a plus-one, address the invitation to “Ms. Lauren Hayes and Guest.” If you know the partner’s name, use it instead: “Ms. Lauren Hayes and Mr. Thomas Rivera.” Adults-Only Weddings If children are not invited, the most polite approach is through addressing. Write only the adults’ names on the envelope. Adding “No Children” to the invitation can read as unwelcoming. If you want to be explicit, include a gentle note on your wedding website or details card: “We respectfully request an adults-only evening.” Some couples offer childcare referrals as a courtesy, which goes a long way. Separate Invitations for Adult Children Adult children (generally 18 and older) living at home may receive their own invitation, especially if they are being offered a plus-one. If they are not getting a plus-one, including their name on the family invitation is perfectly fine. International and Long-Distance Guests Send invitations to international guests 12 weeks ahead. Include supplementary travel information on your wedding website: visa requirements, airport details, recommended hotels, and local transportation options. For guests who may not speak the primary language, consider including a brief translation or a link to translated event details online. Modern vs. Traditional: Updated Rules for 2026 Wedding etiquette evolves. The rules your parents followed still apply in formal settings, but 2026 couples have more flexibility than ever. Digital Invitations: When They Work Digital invitations are fully appropriate for casual weddings, second weddings, elopement receptions, and smaller celebrations. They are also an excellent choice for destination weddings where the guest list is tech-savvy and you want to keep logistics (travel details, RSVP, and itinerary) in a single digital hub. Where digital invitations are less appropriate: ultra-formal black-tie events and religious ceremonies with older, more traditional guest lists. In those cases, a printed invitation remains the standard. Hybrid Paper and Digital Strategies Many couples in 2026 use a hybrid approach: printed invitations for the main guest list, with a digital RSVP option. This pairs the tactile elegance of paper with the convenience of online tracking. Add a QR code to your RSVP card or details card that links directly to your wedding website, where guests can respond and view all event details in one place. Another hybrid approach is sending printed invitations to close family and older relatives while using digital invitations for friends and coworkers. This respects generational preferences without doubling your stationery budget. Bridging paper and digital: If you are sending printed invitations but want the convenience of digital RSVPs, consider adding a QR code to your response card that links guests to your online RSVP page . With Joy, every response feeds into the same guest list, whether it arrives by mail or online, so you have one unified view of who is coming. Casual and Non-Traditional Wording Not every couple wants formal phrasing. Here are some modern alternatives that still feel polished: “Join us as we say I do” (casual, warm) “We are getting married and want you there” (direct, joyful) “Dinner, dancing, and the best day ever” (playful, party-forward) The key is consistency. Match your invitation tone to the event itself. A backyard barbecue wedding deserves relaxed wording; a ballroom reception calls for something more refined. Eco-Friendly Invitation Options Sustainable invitations are a growing trend. Options include seed paper (which guests can plant after the wedding), recycled cardstock, soy-based inks, and fully digital suites. None of these choices are considered an etiquette breach. In fact, many guests appreciate the thoughtfulness. Dress Code Guidance on Invitations If your celebration has a specific dress code, communicate it on the details card or the lower right corner of the invitation. Common phrasing includes: Black Tie: “Black Tie” or “Black Tie Invited” Formal: “Formal Attire” or “Black Tie Optional” Semi-Formal: “Cocktail Attire” or “Semi-Formal Attire” Casual: “Dressy Casual” or “Garden Party Attire” If your event has a theme or setting that affects clothing choices (a beach ceremony, a rustic barn, or an outdoor summer celebration), mention it briefly so guests can dress comfortably. Your wedding website is the best place to expand on dress code details, outfit inspiration, and weather notes. What Not to Put on a Wedding Invitation Some things belong on your wedding website, not your invitation. Keep these off the main card: Registry information: Listing where you are registered on the invitation is generally considered poor form. Direct guests to your wedding website, where they can find your gift registry naturally. Accommodation details: Save hotel blocks and travel logistics for the details card or your wedding website. Meal choices: These belong on the RSVP card or your digital RSVP form, not the invitation itself. “No boxed gifts” or cash requests: This comes across as presumptuous regardless of how it is phrased. Let your registry speak for itself. Social media hashtags: Include these on signage at the venue, not on the formal invitation. Common Mistakes to Avoid Even well-planned couples trip up on these details. Watch out for: Misspelling guest names: Double-check every name before printing. There is no faster way to offend a guest than misspelling their name on an invitation. Forgetting postage on RSVP envelopes: An unstamped return envelope reduces response rates dramatically. Inconsistent formality: If your invitation uses formal wording, the RSVP card and details card should match that tone. Missing the RSVP deadline on the card: Always print a specific date. “Kindly respond” with no deadline guarantees late responses. Ordering too few invitations: Order 10 to 15% more than your guest count. You will need extras for keepsakes, last-minute additions, and printing errors. Not proofing the final print: Request a physical proof before the full run. Digital previews do not catch color or alignment issues the same way. Sending invitations to people who did not get a save-the-date: If someone received a save-the-date, they must receive a formal invitation. The reverse does not apply, so it is fine to add guests at the invitation stage who did not get a save-the-date. Addressing to “The Smith Family” and leaving it vague: Name every invited person. Ambiguous addressing leads to surprise plus-ones and children you were not planning on. Your Invitation Is Only the Beginning A beautiful invitation sets the tone, but it is one piece of a larger experience. Your wedding website is where guests go for everything the invitation cannot hold: directions, hotel blocks, registry links, dress code details, the full weekend itinerary, and your love story. Think of the invitation as the opening line and the wedding website as the rest of the conversation. When both are set up early, your stationery suite works as a system: save-the-dates link to the website, invitations point guests to RSVP online, and every detail lives in one place that guests can revisit any time. Joy makes this easy. Your free wedding website goes live in minutes, and it is designed to complement your paper stationery, not replace it. Set it up when you send save-the-dates so guests have a single destination from day one. Frequently Asked Questions How far in advance should wedding invitations be sent? Send wedding invitations 6 to 8 weeks before a local wedding and 10 to 12 weeks before a destination wedding. Save-the-dates should go out 6 to 8 months in advance (up to 12 months for destination events). Whose name goes first on a wedding invitation? There is no single correct answer. Traditional etiquette placed the bride’s name first, and many couples still follow that convention. Others list names alphabetically or in whichever order sounds best. The choice is yours. Is it rude not to give a plus-one on a wedding invitation? It is not rude to limit plus-ones, but married, engaged, and cohabiting couples should always be invited together. For single guests, plus-ones depend on budget and venue capacity. Guests who will not know anyone else at the wedding are good candidates for a plus-one. Do you put registry information on a wedding invitation? It is best to keep registry information off the wedding invitation itself. Instead, list your registries on your wedding website. Guests will naturally look there, and close family members can spread the word informally. Are digital wedding invitations acceptable? Yes. Digital wedding invitations are appropriate for casual and semi-formal weddings, second weddings, elopement receptions, and events with tech-savvy guest lists. For ultra-formal or very traditional affairs, printed invitations remain the standard. How do you address a wedding invitation to a married couple with different last names? List each person with their own title and full name: “Ms. Lauren Hayes and Mr. David Chen.” Place both names on the same line connected by “and.” On the inner envelope (if used), write their first names: “Lauren and David.” Do you have to invite everyone who received a save-the-date? Yes. A save-the-date is a promise that a formal invitation will follow. Retracting an invitation after sending a save-the-date is a serious etiquette breach. Only send save-the-dates to guests you are certain will make the final guest list. What is the correct stacking order for a wedding invitation suite? Stack items face-up from largest to smallest: invitation on the bottom, then the reception card, details card, and RSVP card with its envelope on top. If using an inner envelope, slide the stack in with text facing the back flap.

title: Does AvePoint Back Up Monday.com?
summary: Learn how AvePoint provides automated, full-fidelity backup, granular restore, and longer retention beyond native recovery options.
body_text: Yes, AvePoint backs up monday.com. AvePoint provides automated, full-fidelity backup for items, sub-items, update and comment history, status, people, and other metadata, with item-level restore. It complements monday.com ’ s native recovery capabilities with additional backup, retention, and granular restore options for critical project data and history. Key Takeaways AvePoint provides full-fidelity backup and granular restore for monday.com. Coverage extends beyond native recovery options and helps preserve critical project data and history. Native recovery has retention and recovery limitations. Deleted items remain recoverable for roughly 30 days, while some content types have more limited native recovery options. Recovery should extend beyond the default retention window. AvePoint’s monday.com backups default to seven years of retention and can be adjusted to align with organizational compliance requirements. Monday.com does not operate in isolation. Most organizations use it alongside Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, creating a need for consistent backup, retention, and recovery policies across multiple SaaS platforms. Multicloud coverage reduces operational complexity. AvePoint protects monday.com alongside Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace under a single backup and recovery platform. AI and automation increase the impact of data loss. As automations and AI-generated summaries depend on board data and metadata, backup gaps can affect downstream processes and reporting accuracy. Recovery readiness matters as much as backup coverage. Regular restore testing helps validate that recovery processes will work when needed and provides evidence for audit and compliance requirements. Why Does Monday.com Need Independent Backup? Monday.com needs independent backup because deleted updates and comments have more limited native recovery options, deleted items become permanently unrecoverable after a matter of weeks, and native exports miss workflow logic, relationships, and configuration context entirely. While monday.com runs internal daily backups, it strongly recommends a third-party backup solution for customers who need capabilities like point-in-time restore, automated backups, and granular restore beyond the native options. While there are no major public stories of data breaches or data loss with regard to monday.com, 68% of organizations experience some form of data loss annually, and up to 29% occurred because of human error . Simple actions like deleting an update or comment result in instant and permanent deletion. Even in cases where there is a recycle bin, deleted items are no longer recoverable through the platform after 30 days . The risk increases when considering bulk actions like data imports or syncs with third-party apps. Deleting comments or updates. Once an update or comment is deleted, it is no longer available through native recovery options. 30 Day recycle bin limit. Deleted items become permanently unrecoverable after 30 days. Native exports miss context. Manual exports and recovery options often miss workflow logic, relationships, and configuration context, making clean recovery difficult even within the window. API limitations exclude key data. Certain data types, including views, activity logs, dashboards, and automations, can’t be backed up at all due to platform API limitations. How Does AvePoint Back Up Monday.com? AvePoint backs up monday.com with full-fidelity, automated protection covering items, sub-items, and the metadata native tools leave exposed: full update and comment history, status, people, date, and text fields, restoring a single item or sub-item without touching the rest of the board. What’s protected: Items, sub-items, and critical metadata, full update/comment history, status, people, date, and text fields, beyond what monday.com’s own activity logs and undo functions cover Restore: Non-destructive restore recreates deleted items, updates, and comments as new objects, preserving project history without overwriting existing data. Backup frequency: Automated, running up to four times a day for a low recovery point objective, instead of relying on manual export/import Retention: Defaults to seven years and can be adjusted up or down to match compliance needs Granularity: A single item or sub-item restoration without affecting the rest of the board, avoiding board-wide recovery operations How Does AvePoint’s Monday.com Backup Compare to Native Recovery? AvePoint’s monday.com backup differs from native recovery most on what’s recoverable at all: Native recovery options vary by content type and retention window, while AvePoint restores items, sub-items, and their associated history with policy-based retention and granular recovery options. Capability Monday.com Native AvePoint Data protected Platform-level backup only; user/item recovery limited to activity logs and basic undo Items, sub-items, full update/comment history, status, people, date, and text fields Restore Very limited; relies on activity logs and undo history, no point-in-time recovery. Advanced Recovery Scenarios require Monday.com support. Granular and non-destructive; recovers full update/comment threads as new objects Retention Data permanently deleted after 30 Days from Recycle Bin. No recovery for deleted updates and comments. Internal backups deleted after 25 days Defaults to 7 years, adjustable to your compliance needs Backup frequency Once daily Automated, up to 4 times a day Granularity No granular recovery of a single item or sub-item Item- and sub-item-level restore, including full update history Management overhead High: manual export/import required to recover specific items or historical states Low: centralized management and audit-ready reporting What Does This Mean for Monday.com Alongside Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace? Monday.com rarely runs alone. Teams pair it with Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace for documents and communication, and both carry native-recovery gaps of their own. AvePoint backs up monday.com alongside Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and other SaaS applications under one platform, instead of one retention policy and restore process per tool. Treating monday.com backup as a standalone project misses the point. A team managing recovery for monday.com, SharePoint, and Google Drive under separate native recovery windows is carrying separate sets of retention rules and restore limitations for every platform, not one. How Does AI and Automation Change the Stakes of Monday.com Data Loss? As teams build automations and connect AI tools to monday.com boards for status reporting and planning, losing update history or item metadata doesn’t just erase a record, it silently breaks whatever automation or AI-generated summary depended on that structure. A backup gap in monday.com used to be a project-visibility problem. Once automations and AI summaries run on top of that same board data, it’s also a reliability problem for every downstream process built on it. Monday.com Backup Maturity Tiers Tier What It Looks Like Tier 1: Native only Relying solely on monday.com’s activity logs and undo history. Deleted comments/updates unrecoverable instantly; deleted items unrecoverable after 30 days. Tier 2: Partial coverage Native recovery supplemented by manual exports for a few critical boards. Workflow logic and relationships still lost on export; no automation. Tier 3: AvePoint-backed, multi-platform Automated backup with item- and sub-item-level restore, full update history preserved, retention set by policy, and coverage extended across monday.com, Microsoft 365, and Google Workspace under one platform. AvePoint backs up monday.com alongside Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Salesforce under one platform, with item-level restore and retention set by your organization, not a native default. Frequently Asked Questions Can I recover a deleted comment or update in monday.com? Deleting an update or comment in monday.com is unrecoverable through standard recovery tools; there is no trash, undo, or native recovery path for that content type at all without a third-party backup. How long do I have to recover a deleted item in monday.com? Deleted items in monday.com become permanently unrecoverable through the platform after roughly 30 days, after which native recovery is no longer possible. Does AvePoint’s monday.com backup replace native recovery or work alongside it? AvePoint’s monday.com backup works alongside native recovery, closing the gaps in comment/update recovery, retention, and granularity that native tools leave open rather than replacing them outright. How often should I test a monday.com restore? Test a monday.com restore at least quarterly, and align the schedule to an organization’s audit or compliance review cycle so recovery evidence stays current. title: 2026 INEOS Grenadier Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: The upscale INEOS Grenadier off-roader, with Land Rover looks and BMW power, returns for 2026 with a couple of enhanced features and a new trim.
body_text: The INEOS Grenadier was introduced to the North American market as a 2024 model. Named after a pub in London and built as a spiritual successor to old-school 4X4s, the Grenadier targets vehicles such as the Ford Bronco, the Jeep Wrangler, the Land Rover Defender, the Toyota Land Cruiser, and the Mercedes-Benz G-Class. The 2026 INEOS Grenadier Station SUV has four trims: Grenadier, Fieldmaster, Trialmaster, and Black Edition. 2026 INEOS Grenadier Pricing, Specs, and Release Date What’s New for the 2026 INEOS Grenadier Design Powertrain Interior Technology Safety Pricing and Release Date Further Research What’s New for the 2026 INEOS Grenadier Since the INEOS Grenadier was all-new in 2024, it didn’t receive any significant changes in 2025, so 2026 is the first year the model gets any notable updates. The biggest change is to the steering box hardware, which tightens the turning radius and improves on-road steering. Other significant changes include an improved HVAC system for faster heating and cooling, updated advanced driver-assistance systems, and a new Black Edition trim. Design The INEOS Grenadier has an upright, boxy stance reminiscent of the original Land Rover Defender, which isn’t surprising, since that vehicle was the inspiration for the Grenadier. It has a body-on-frame chassis, safari windows, flared fenders, and beefy all-terrain tires. Standard wheels are 17-inch steelies, but 17-inch alloys and 18-inch steel wheels are also available. In addition to the new Black Edition, the other Grenadier trims are available with a Black Pack that includes black grille strips, black roof rails, and dark front and rear skid plates. Powertrain The 2026 Grenadier is equipped with a BMW turbocharged 3.0-liter inline six-cylinder engine that delivers 282 horsepower and 332 pound-feet of torque. This is paired with an eight-speed ZF automatic transmission. This vehicle has permanent four-wheel drive (4WD), a two-speed transfer case, and a center differential lock. The Trailmaster trim, designed for the most extreme off-road conditions, also offers front- and rear-locking differentials. The EPA estimates that most Grenadier trims will get 15 mpg in the city and on the highway, while the Trailmaster will deliver 14 mpg in both situations. Maximum towing capacity is about 7,700 pounds. Interior Stepping inside an INEOS Grenadier almost feels like stepping into the cockpit of an airplane with all the switches and dials on the roof and the center console. Recaro seats are standard, with seating surfaces made from a mix of easy-to-clean cloth and vinyl. Black and gray leather options are available, depending on the trim. Though the Grenadier doesn’t come with a traditional moonroof, it does offer safari windows—standard on the Fieldmaster and available on other trims—which consist of two manually removable glass panels above the driver and passenger seats. The Grenadier Wagon seats five, and has 40.6 cubic feet of cargo space behind the second-row seats. Maximum cargo space is 71.8 cubic feet when the rear seats are folded flat. Technology The 2026 Grenadier comes standard with a 12.3-inch infotainment screen controlled by touch or a rotary dial, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, LED headlights, and USB-A and USB-C ports. Our favorite feature is the “toot” button, which is a softer, more polite horn meant to warn cyclists and pedestrians. Available tech features include heated power-adjustable exterior mirrors, heated windshield washer jets, puddle lamps, ambient lighting, and a compass with an altimeter. A premium sound system option adds a subwoofer and an uprated amplifier to the base system. One of the coolest tech features is the standard Pathfinder navigation system, which allows drivers to follow an existing GPX file (Follow Path), record a new GPX file (Record Path), or manually record a route (Roadbook). Front parking sensors are the only real available safety feature. Features that are not available on the 2026 Grenadier include blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control, lane-keep assist, and a surround-view camera system. Neither the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) nor the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) had crash-tested the INEOS Grenadier at the time of writing. Pricing and Release Date The 2026 INEOS Grenadier went on sale in January of 2026. At the time of writing, the starting price for the base Grenadier was $72,995 including a $1,995 destination charge. The Fieldmaster and Trailmaster both start at $80,995, and the Black Edition rounds out the lineup with a starting price of $84,995. In addition to the available wheels, package options, and accessories, it’s worth noting that the only free color the only free color on the Grenadier is Britannia Blue. All other colors cost $995. title: WhatsApp Template Message API: A Complete 2026 Guide
summary: Zoko is an all-in-one system that leverages the WhatsApp API to help you do business, on WhatsApp. Go beyond chatting - reach customers, enable product discovery, collect payments, get feedback - all on WhatsApp.
body_text: A WhatsApp message template is a pre-approved message format that Meta reviews before you can send it. If you're using the WhatsApp Business API (now built entirely on Meta's Cloud API), templates are the only way to message a customer when you don't have an open service window, meaning the customer hasn't messaged you recently. This exists for one reason: WhatsApp doesn't want businesses spamming people the way email and SMS lists often do. So instead of letting any company send any message at any time, Meta requires that all business-initiated messages, order updates, shipping alerts, cart reminders, and promotions go through a template that's been submitted, categorised, and approved in advance. If you only remember one thing from this piece, remember this: the moment you want to message a customer first, instead of replying to them, you need a template. Everything else (categories, approval, cost, rejection reasons) flows from that one rule. ‍ Why Does This Trip Up So Many Merchants ‍ Most confusion around the template API comes from three places: Not knowing when a template is required. If a customer messages you first, you get a free-form reply window (commonly referred to as the 24-hour service window). Anything you send after that window closes, or anything you send to start a conversation, needs to be approved by a template. Picking the wrong category. Meta sorts every template into one of three types, and picking the wrong one is the single most common reason templates get rejected or, worse, silently reclassified after you've already been using them. Assuming approval is guaranteed or instant. Meta reviews every submission. Review times are commonly quick, but they're not fixed, and approval is never guaranteed — Meta can also reclassify or restrict templates after the fact if the content doesn't match how you've categorised it. ‍ The Three Template Categories ‍ Every template you submit gets assigned one of these categories: Utility : Transactional, non-promotional updates that the customer is already expecting as a result of something they did: order confirmations, shipping updates, delivery alerts, account notifications. These typically face the lowest approval friction and are priced lower than marketing templates. Marketing : Anything designed to drive sales or re-engagement: promotions, offers, product launches, newsletters, abandoned-cart nudges. These are subject to greater scrutiny, cost more, and require clear opt-in from the recipient. Authentication : One-time passcodes and identity verification messages. Narrow use case, tightly formatted. A simple test that's commonly used to sort a message: would this message exist without something the customer already did? If yes, it's likely Utility. If the goal is to get them to do something new (buy, re-engage, click), it's Marketing. Getting this wrong isn't just a risk of rejection. Businesses that repeatedly mislabel promotional content as Utility (to dodge marketing pricing or opt-in requirements) risk warnings, rate limits, or template restrictions from Meta. This is a compliance issue, not a technicality — treat it that way. ‍ How Approval Actually Works ‍ You submit a template — the copy, any variables, buttons, media — through the API or your provider's template manager. Meta reviews it against its WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy and either approves it, rejects it, or occasionally flags it for further review. A few practical notes worth knowing before you submit: Keep dynamic variables (like {{1}}, {{2}}) minimal, and don't open a message with a variable or fill the entire body with them — templates that look like Hi {{1}}, here is {{2}} read as spam patterns by Meta's reviewers and are commonly rejected. Add static, human framing around variables instead: something like "Your order #{{1}} has shipped. Track it here: {{2}}." If a template is rejected but you believe it's categorised correctly, most providers offer a way to request a review rather than resubmitting from scratch. Pricing is also tied to category and recipient country, and it changes based on Meta's rate card — so avoid treating any specific number as fixed. What's stable is the pattern: Utility and Authentication templates are consistently priced lower than Marketing templates, and free-form replies within an open service window don't carry a per-message template cost. One more thing merchants running promotions should know: Meta caps the number of marketing templates a single person can receive across all businesses in a day, not just from you. If your message gets blocked for this reason, sending more volume won't fix it — better targeting and timing will. ‍ Where Merchants Actually Get Stuck This is rarely a coding problem. It's an operations problem. Most Shopify merchants don't have someone whose full-time job is watching template statuses, correcting rejected categories, tracking which templates are tied to which flow, and making sure marketing sends only go to people who've actually opted in. When that falls on a founder or a lean ops team on top of running the store, templates get miscategorised, sends get blocked, and nobody notices until a customer complains or a number gets restricted. This is also where the "just use the raw API" path gets expensive in time, even when it's free in dollars. Someone still has to build the submission workflow, track approval states, and keep marketing sends compliant with opt-in rules — every week, indefinitely. ‍ Where Does This Fit into a Shopify WhatsApp Setup Once you're clear on categories, the practical question becomes: how do you actually run this without manually managing templates for every order update, cart reminder, and promotion? This is where the category should shape the tool, not the other way around. Order confirmations, shipping updates, and COD confirmations are Utility-style messages — in Zoko , these are typically handled through Flows , which trigger the right message automatically off Shopify order events instead of someone submitting and monitoring a template by hand. Promotional sends (the Marketing category) are where Broadcasts with Segments matter, since a targeted, permissioned list is what keeps a marketing template's engagement (and approval standing) healthy in the first place. The reason native Shopify integration matters here specifically: your order and customer data are already structured and synced, so the right template fires off the right trigger without a developer wiring up custom webhooks for each event. And because Zoko operates as an official Meta Business Partner, category and compliance groundwork (opt-in handling, template structure guidance) is built into the workflow rather than something your team has to independently police. None of this replaces Meta's approval process — no provider controls that. What a Shopify-native platform can do is reduce the amount of compliance and category logic that sits on your team's shoulders day-to-day. ‍ In-house Cloud API vs. a Shopify-Native Platform ‍ If you have an engineering team and your business requires highly customised messaging logic, integrating directly with Meta's Cloud API can be a viable option. It gives you complete control over template creation, webhook handling, message routing, and backend integrations. For businesses building proprietary systems or managing multiple internal applications, that flexibility can be valuable. However, for most Shopify merchants, the integration itself isn't the biggest challenge—maintaining it is. Every new template needs to be created, categorised correctly, submitted for approval, and monitored over time. Marketing campaigns require valid customer opt-ins, while transactional workflows need to stay synchronised with order events. If templates are rejected, paused, or reclassified, someone on your team must identify the issue, make corrections, and resubmit them. As your catalogue, campaigns, and customer base grow, those operational tasks quickly become recurring responsibilities rather than one-time setups. A Shopify-native platform removes much of that overhead by connecting your store data, customer information, and WhatsApp workflows out of the box. Instead of building custom webhooks for every order event, merchants can automate common journeys—such as abandoned cart recovery, order confirmations, shipping updates, COD verification, and post-purchase follow-ups—using pre-built workflows that stay connected to Shopify. For businesses focused on growing sales rather than maintaining infrastructure, this approach shifts the effort from managing the API to optimising customer conversations. Platforms like Zoko combine native Shopify integration, automation, and Meta-compliant messaging in one place, allowing merchants to scale WhatsApp operations without building and maintaining the underlying infrastructure themselves. ‍ The Bottom Line The WhatsApp Template Message API is more than a technical requirement—it's the foundation of compliant, scalable business messaging on WhatsApp. By understanding when templates are required, choosing the right category, and following Meta's approval process, businesses can automate customer communication without compromising trust or risking policy violations. For Shopify merchants, the bigger opportunity is turning approved templates into automated customer journeys. When order updates, abandoned cart reminders, COD confirmations, and promotional campaigns are triggered automatically through a Shopify-native platform like Zoko , WhatsApp becomes more than a messaging channel—it becomes a revenue-driving commerce engine that scales with your business. ‍ FAQs ‍ 1. Do I need a template for every WhatsApp message? No. If a customer messages you first, you can reply free-form within the open service window. Templates are required when you're initiating the conversation or messaging after that window closes. ‍ 2. How long does template approval take? Review times are commonly fast, often within a day, but Meta doesn't publish a fixed guarantee, and timing can vary by submission. ‍ 3. Can a template get reclassified after it's approved? Yes. Meta can review and reassign a template's category later if the content doesn't match how it's been used, which is another reason to categorise accurately upfront rather than to save on marketing pricing. ‍ 4. Is Marketing more expensive than Utility? Generally, yes, though exact rates depend on Meta's current category-specific pricing and the recipient's country, so it's worth checking the current rates rather than relying on a fixed figure. ‍ 5. Can I use the same WhatsApp template in multiple languages? No. Each language version of a template must be submitted separately for Meta's approval. While the structure and variables can remain the same, the translated content is reviewed independently to ensure it complies with WhatsApp's messaging policies and accurately reflects the intended category. ‍ 6. Can I delete a WhatsApp template I no longer use? Yes. Businesses can delete unused templates from their WhatsApp Business account or through their Business Solution Provider. Removing outdated templates helps keep your template library organised, although deleting a template doesn't affect messages that have already been delivered. ‍ 7. Can I include product links in WhatsApp template messages? Yes, provided the links comply with Meta's policies and are relevant to the template's purpose. For ecommerce businesses, it's common to include links to product pages, checkout pages, order tracking, or payment pages within approved templates using dynamic variables where appropriate. ‍ 8. What happens if my WhatsApp template is rejected? If Meta rejects a template, you'll receive a reason for the rejection. In most cases, you can edit the content, correct the category if necessary, and resubmit it for review. Some Business Solution Providers also allow you to request a review if you believe the template was incorrectly rejected. ‍ 9. Do I need coding knowledge to use WhatsApp template messages? Not necessarily. While businesses using Meta's Cloud API directly may need technical expertise, many Business Solution Providers offer visual interfaces for creating, submitting, and managing templates. Shopify-native platforms like Zoko also let merchants automate template messages through no-code workflows instead of custom development.

title: Meet the Hilton Garden Inn Busselton Team Bringing Brighthearted Hospitality to Life
summary: Go behind the scenes with the next installment of Hilton's Behind the Stay series, spotlighting Hilton Garden Inn Busselton team.
body_text: Listen to this article 0:00 On Western Australia's stunning coastline, one hotel has become the gathering place where thoughtful service leads to unforgettable memories Go behind the scenes with the next installment of Hilton's Behind the Stay series, spotlighting the remarkable team members whose passion and dedication make Hilton the World's Best Place to Stay. Discover how the Hilton Garden Inn Busselton team transforms everyday stays into meaningful experiences through Brighthearted hospitality, genuine local connections and heartfelt service. Meet the people who have helped turn this waterfront hotel into a beloved Australian destination where visitors and locals alike discover the heart behind every stay. Overlooking the turquoise waters of Geographe Bay and the iconic Busselton Jetty, Hilton Garden Inn Busselton boasts one of Western Australia's most picturesque coastal settings. But while the breathtaking scenery and iconic waterfront location make an amazing first impression, it's the warmth of the team that guests remember most fondly. Hilton Garden Inn Busselton - Exterior Team members here are united around a commitment to make the hotel more than just a place to stay. Rooted in Hilton Garden Inn's Brighthearted hospitality service philosophy, which encourages team members to deliver service that is sincere, lighthearted and polished through every interaction, the team has built genuine relationships with guests and the local community alike. The goal is to provide a dose of positivity that makes every stay better and brighter, and as a result, they create guest experiences that are thoughtful, memorable and personalised. Stepping inside, guests are greeted by warm team members like Assistant Front Office Manager Ntula, who has lived in the Southwest region her entire life and witnessed Busselton’s transformation from a quiet coastal town into a thriving tourism destination. She has also watched the hotel evolve into a gathering place where locals come to enjoy the view, meet friends and experience their hometown from an entirely new perspective. For local Joan, the kindness she experienced during a difficult chapter of her life turned Hilton Garden Inn Busselton into a place of genuine comfort. Today, she's a familiar face whose regular visits reflect the glowing connections the team has built with visitors and locals alike. title: Jobs Report and Drop in Unemployment Boost Markets
summary: Cboe Global Markets, a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
body_text: Article Published at 9:20 a.m. CT. JJ Kinahan is Senior Vice President, Head of Retail Expansion and Alternative Investment Products at Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe). Key Takeaways: Markets could be volatile amid softness in job growth Job numbers diminish rate hike scenario Honeywell Aerospace reports weak results, shares tumble The surprise jobs report gave the markets an early boost that may be tough to hold on to throughout a summer Friday when many folks tend to cut the work-day hours. July nonfarm payrolls slumped by 23,000 jobs, a big miss from an expectation of an 83,000 gain, and June and July’s numbers were significantly revised downward. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. Though the drop in unemployment is usually considered a plus, this one came with a decline to 61.4% in participation, the lowest level in more than five years, meaning fewer folks are looking for jobs. The numbers also mitigate the rate hike scenario, but as traders absorb the news – that we don’t have job growth -- we could see some volatility in the markets. In early trading, the S&P 500 Index was up 0.32% while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.90%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was edging higher by 0.15%. The Trade Desk shares tumbled 23% in early trading after yesterday’s dismal earnings report and outlook for the ad-tech firm. The company blamed the profits and revenue drops on weaker consumer spending, tariffs and higher oil prices. A lack of catalysts pushed the markets into the red yesterday, ending a rally that seemed like it might have more legs. Higher oil prices smacked market optimism as the proposed passage deal to open shipping through the Strait of Hormuz seemed unworkable. WTI Crude Oil prices, which were treading lower in the $75-per-barrel range in recent sessions, rose 2.8% to close around $77 a barrel. In early trading, they were 0.31% lower. That, plus mixed earnings results from a handful companies, cut into market sentiment, pushing all three major indices to the downside. The Dow fell off its five-day record-breaking perch, closing lower by 0.85% while the S&P 500 fell 0.18% and the Nasdaq slipped about 0.06%. Honeywell Aerospace was among the biggest culprits on the Nasdaq and S&P 500, tumbling 23.2% after reporting second-quarter earnings and sales that missed Wall Street’s expectations in it first reporting quarter after June’s spinoff from Honeywell Technologies. Adding to the off-putting results was a softer-than-expected forecast that cut full-year sales growth expectations from 4% to 5%, off earlier guidance of 7% to 9%. In early trading, shares were recovering by 1.5%. SpaceX shares managed to move ahead yesterday, resisting the “lock-up dump” that can occur when share lockups expire. Not surprisingly, trading volume was more than 110% higher than normal given the much larger float after 911 million new shares were available for trading. The upside might be considered a signal that many of the employees and early investors chose to hang on to their shares. But Day 1 does not make a long-term trend and we could see some resistance if the stock returns to its initial public offering level. Shares were up 3.6% to $119, still notably off from its $135 IPO price and the $225 peak in the first week of trading. Wendy’s shares slumped 3.7% in early trading after reporting a 7% drop in same-store sales and an 8.2% retreat in system-wide sales amid a slowdown in consumer spending. As a result, the maker of square hamburgers and Frosty’s withdrew its guidance and scratched its dividend, choosing instead to invest in initiatives to build the brand.
